issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) specify acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity), but the implemented solution (and the example usage in the template Main) define/expect a three-parameter method (ingredient name, price, quantity). This is a method parameter mismatch that will confuse students about the required signature and parameters to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across all artifacts. Either update the problem statement/UML to require three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity) or change the solution/template to implement/illustrate the four-parameter method (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity). Also update example usages in Main accordingly.

issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize the stock attribute in the SealSaloon constructor, but also states that the stock attribute must be static (and UML implies a shared stock). Initializing a static final field in an instance constructor is invalid in Java; the solution instead declares and initializes a private static final Stock at declaration. This creates a contradiction in where and how students are told to initialize the shared stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design: if stock is intended to be shared across all SealSaloon instances, state that it should be declared static (and if immutable, static final) and initialized at declaration or in a static initializer. Remove or correct the instruction that stock should be initialized in the instance constructor. Update the problem statement and UML to match the implementation approach.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters including a supplier name (acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int) / supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity). Both the template usage (Main.java) and the provided solution implement and call acceptSupplyDelivery with three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch between the documented signature and the code can confuse students about the required method signature and parameter roles.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to specify the three-parameter signature (acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity)) or change the code to implement the four-parameter signature (acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity)) and handle or store the supplierName as appropriate. Ensure examples in Main.java and the UML/signature in the problem text match the chosen signature.
